title: Recovering from a Bad Cold
script: Narrator: [weak] Four days ago, I woke up with a sore throat and a heavy, aching head.
Narrator: [groaning] By the afternoon, a fever had settled in, and my whole body felt strangely weak.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I almost forced myself to go to work anyway, the way I usually do when I feel unwell.
Narrator: [reflective] But something made me stop that morning. I realized I was only going to make things worse.
Narrator: [determined] So I called my supervisor, explained honestly, and stayed home to rest instead of pushing myself.
Narrator: [caring] I drank warm water with lemon and honey, and I kept a blanket close all day.
Narrator: [honest] Sleep came easily that first day. My body seemed to know exactly what it needed most.
Narrator: [grateful] My sister heard I was sick and brought warm soup to my door every single evening.
Narrator: [warmly] That small kindness meant more to me than she probably realized at the time.
Narrator: [thoughtful] By the second day, my fever was still there, but my headache had softened a little.
Narrator: [honest] I tried to read a book, but my eyes felt tired, so I mostly just rested quietly.
Narrator: [hopeful] On the third day, I woke up and noticed my throat did not hurt as much.
Narrator: [relieved] I still felt tired, but a different kind of tired, more like healing than sickness.
Narrator: [reflective] I used that time to think, too, about how rarely I actually let myself slow down.
Narrator: [honest] Normally I push through everything, even when my body is clearly asking me to stop.
Narrator: [warmly] Today, four days later, I finally feel like myself again, with real energy returning slowly.
Narrator: [grateful] My sister's soup, my own patience, and simple rest brought me back faster than I expected.
Narrator: [reflective] I learned something important this week. Resting properly is not laziness, it is simply how the body heals.
Narrator: [peacefully] Next time I feel sick, I hope I remember this lesson instead of ignoring my body again.
Narrator: [with a small smile] Tomorrow, I plan to return to work, grateful, rested, and finally breathing easily again.
